title: HSM interop patterns and Terraform staging matrix (v0.1 rough)
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is a working sketch of HSM/KMS interoperability patterns for on-prem and VPC Private deployments, and a proposed Terraform module staging matrix to support safe upgrades. The goal is to capture pragmatic rails we can use for customers migrating from software KMS->cloud KMS connectors->HSM-backed KMS, and to outline testing/rollback and audit expectations for each stage.

High‑level patterns (TL;DR):
- Proxy mode: operator deploys an HSM-backed KMS (vendor-specific) behind a small proxy shim that implements Redwood's KMS API surface. Useful for quick cutovers and when customer HSMs don’t speak our full API.
- Envelope-only mode: Redwood stores encrypted envelopes; customer holds KEKs in HSM and returns wrapped DEKs. Lower surface area but requires more orchestration in bootstrap flows.
- Attested node mode: nodes use TPM/SGX to attest and pull per‑node keys from HSM; recommended for high-assurance customers with airgap/offline requirements.

Key risks we track:
- Key availability: HSM firmware upgrades, quorum changes, or network partition can render keys unavailable.
- Key compromise of operator-managed proxies in multi-tenant setups (mitigate via attestation + split keystores).
- Terraform drift vs hardware state (manual HSM config is common).
- Audit fidelity: vendor audit logs often have different schemas and retention defaults.

Staging matrix (states and acceptance gates)

We propose the following discrete stages for each customer rollout. Each stage is represented by a Terraform module variable/flag and accompanied by a test checklist and rollback path.

0. baseline (software KMS)
- Description: Customer uses our default software KMS or cloud KMS; no HSM involved.
- Terraform flag: module.kms.mode = "software"
- Acceptance: smoke tokens, E2E inference with secrets resolver enabled, sample audit events emitted.
- Rollback: standard module reapply to mode="software".

1. proxy-read (HSM present behind read-only proxy)
- Description: HSM is accessible; proxy can read wrapped keys for decryption but not enroll or unwrap new KEKs. Useful for read migration testing.
- Terraform flag: module.kms.mode = "proxy"; module.kms.proxy_read_only = true
- Acceptance tests: decrypt existing envelopes, verify latency SLO for decrypt (< 2x baseline), audit events show HSM partial responses.
- Rollback: flip proxy_read_only=false -> software mode fallback if latency or errors exceed threshold.

2. proxy-full (HSM proxy for wrap/unwrap)
- Description: Proxy handles full lifecycle (wrap/unwrap, key creation) but master KEK is HSM-managed.
- Terraform flag: module.kms.mode = "proxy"; module.kms.proxy_read_only = false
- Acceptance: create new KEK via API, rotate DEK, end-to-end encryption/rotate smoke test, system recovers from simulated HSM transient error.
- Rollback: rotate back to software KMS with DEK rewrap or failover path; see rollback playbook.

3. envelope-only (split envelope, HSM offline-only KEK provider)
- Description: Only KEKs live in HSM; Redwood holds encrypted DEKs and performs operations after HSM unwrap handshake. This minimizes HSM traffic but increases bootstrap complexity.
- Terraform flag: module.kms.mode = "envelope"
- Acceptance: attest+unwrap walk, documented manual recovery steps tested, offline recovery exercise executed.
- Rollback: requires rewrap strategy with original KEK or emergency transfer key (stored in escrow HSM cluster).

4. attested-node (per-node keys + HSM attestation)
- Description: Node-level keys are provisioned after node attestation. High cost but best isolation.
- Terraform flag: module.kms.mode = "attested"; module.kms.attestation_provider = "tpm|sgx"
- Acceptance: attestation flow validated, zero-downtime node replacement tested, node compromise injection tested in lab.
- Rollback: reprovision nodes using previous attestation config and rehydrate DEKs.

Terraform module notes (interface sketch)

We should avoid baking vendor specifics into the main module. Instead expose a small vendor adapter interface and publish vendor-specific submodules: hsm/vendor_x, hsm/vendor_y. The root module will accept an adapter URL or local path variable.

Suggested variables (initial):
- kms_mode (string) -> one of [software, proxy, envelope, attested]
- proxy_endpoint (string) -> url for proxy shim (if mode=proxy)
- hsm_adapter (string) -> path to adapter module (relative or registry)
- audit_forwarding (bool) -> whether to forward HSM logs into our audit pipeline
- audit_topic (string) -> destination pub/sub or file sink
- keystore_escrow (string) -> optional backup KEK identifier
- allowed_admin_principals (list) -> short list of operator/admin principals for Terraform-managed roles

Terraform example snippet (pseudocode):

variable "kms_mode" { default = "software" }
variable "hsm_adapter" { default = "" }

module "kms" {
  source = "../modules/kms-root"
  kms_mode = var.kms_mode
  hsm_adapter = var.hsm_adapter
  audit_forwarding = true
  audit_topic = "projects/redwood-prod/topics/kms-audit"
}

# adapter can be swapped during staged deployments
module "hsm_vendor" {
  source = var.hsm_adapter == "vendor_x" ? "../modules/hsm/vendor_x" : "../modules/hsm/vendor_y"
  admin_list = var.allowed_admin_principals
}

Operational playbook (upgrade + test + rollback)

Pre-flight (operator checklist):
- Confirm HSM firmware & vendor OS versions matched to supported list. Record serials.
- Validate NTP and stable clock (audit timestamps critical).
- Confirm network egress rules from proxy to HSM. Document firewall rules in ticket.
- Export current DEK list and ensure at least one verified backup exists in escrow.
- Inform on-call team and schedule a maintenance window on customer side if needed.

Canary rollout steps:
1) Set kms_mode=proxy and proxy_read_only=true in a staging workspace.
2) Deploy to staging, run the KMS decrypt latency & correctness smoke tests against a dataset of 10k small envelopes.
3) Run HSM outage drill: kill connectivity to HSM for 60s and observe failovers.
4) If successful, enable proxy_full in staging. Run key creation/rotation E2E tests.
5) Promote to canary customer node (lowest impact customer) and monitor 72h.

Monitoring & SLOs to watch during rollout:
- decrypt_error_rate < 0.1%
- decrypt_p95 < baseline*2
- HSM_api_5xx_rate ~ 0 (track vendor error codes separately)
- audit_events_forwarded >= 99%
- terraform_plan_drift events: none for critical resources

Audit integration notes
- Always forward raw vendor logs into our audit pipeline (separate topic), then normalize. Avoid relying solely on normalized events for forensic purposes.
- Tag events with: operator_id, adapter_id, hsm_serial, request_id
- Retention: default 7 days hot, 90 days cold; customers in regulated sectors may require 7 years — provide export & archival playbook.

Hardened rollback patterns
- Soft rollback: flip kms_mode back to software and rewrap DEKs using escrow KEK. This is the fastest path but requires escrow keys to be accessible.
- Recreate proxy with previous adapter image and route traffic back. Keep previous config as immutable artifact in S3/store.
- Emergency HSM loss: use multi-HSM quorum and pre-registered emergency KEKs in an offsite HSM cluster. Document exact quorum steps and phone chain.

Testing / validation matrix (automation targets)
- unit: adapter shim contracts (wrap/unwrap/create/list) mocked tests.
- integration: spin up simulated HSM (vendor simulator) in CI, run 1000 envelope ops at concurrency 50.
- chaos: network partition, cert rotation during live traffic, forced HSM restart.
- compliance: sample audit replay with 3 months of fake traffic to validate retention & export.

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we require HSM attestation chain validation as a gating condition across all customers? (cost vs security tradeoff).
- Should Terraform manage HSM firmware updates? (current stance: no; treat firmware as operational step and document in runbook).
- Decide default audit retention tiers and whether we automatically archive to customer-managed buckets.

Notes from last infra sync (raw):
- Maya: vendor_x provides a TLS-over-ZMQ proxy example; we should standardize the TLS config to mutual TLS with CN mapping to adapter_id.
- Ravi: add a terraform-lint pipeline gate that fails plans touching keystore resources unless approved by keystore-approvers group.
- Lena: build a small shim test harness that can run vendor simulators locally (Docker) for SREs to reproduce enrollment issues.

Appendix: quick manual recovery steps (short)
1) If HSM unreachable: switch Kubernetes secret resolver to cached-mode (serve cached DEKs) for up to 2 hours.
2) If HSM lost permanently: use escrow KEK -> rewrap DEKs into software KMS and rotate application secrets.
3) If audit forwarder fails: keep raw vendor logs on local disk and backfill later to audit_topic; mark incident and page compliance lead.

This is a rough working document. Next actions:
- Assign owner for adapter contract (Ravi).
- Implement vendor simulator harness (Lena).
- Draft Terraform registry layout proposal and open PR for module/adapter separation (Evan).

If anything in this doc contradicts a vendor SLA or existing customer contract, we should escalate before proceeding with rollout.
